questions.prompt: You want to make a table of values to graph \(y = \dfrac{2}{5}x - 3\) on a \([-6, 6]\) grid so that every \(y\)-value is a clean integer (no fractions). Which set of \(x\)-values should you choose?

choices.feedback: Because the slope's denominator is \(5\), picking multiples of \(5\) cancels the fraction cleanly: \(y = -5,\; -3,\; -1\) — all integers that fit inside the \([-6, 6]\) grid.
Careful! You picked multiples of the numerator (\(2\)) instead of the denominator (\(5\)). Plugging in \(x = 2\) gives \(y = \dfrac{4}{5} - 3 = -2\dfrac{1}{5}\), which is a fraction.
The \(-3\) is the \(y\)-intercept, not the denominator of the slope! Plugging in \(x = 3\) gives \(y = \dfrac{6}{5} - 3 = -1\dfrac{4}{5}\), not an integer.
When \(x = 1\), \(y = \dfrac{2}{5}(1) - 3 = -2\dfrac{3}{5}\) — still a fraction! Always choose multiples of the slope's denominator (\(5\)).

questions.prompt:

A negative times a negative is positive! For \(x = -2\), \(y = -\dfrac{3}{2}(-2) + 4 = +3 + 4 = 7\). Now the \(y\)-values \(7,\; 4,\; 1\) decrease steadily by \(3\) every time \(x\) increases by \(2\).
At \(x = 0\), \(y = -\dfrac{3}{2}(0) + 4 = 0 + 4 = +4\), so \((0, 4)\) is right! Look closely at \(x = -2\): a negative times a negative gives \(+3 + 4 = 7\).
You caught that \(x = -2\) is the wrong column, but check the sign: \(-\dfrac{3}{2}(-2) = +3\), and \(+3 + 4 = +7\), not \(-7\).
